note: Platform AI tool schemas as sent to the model. Update deliberately: UPDATE_PLATFORM_AI_TOOL_SNAPSHOT=1 (see registry.test.ts).

function.name: list_metrics
function.description: List the metric definitions you may read here (ids, labels, windows, area). No values. Domain "operations" holds the operational briefing metrics (overall posture, customer-impacting failures, alerts firing, connection health, refresh pipeline, scheduled jobs, data freshness); "incidents" the incident counts; "providers" provider verdicts and call volume. Domain "economics" holds the cost and spend metrics (AI cost, provider cost, operating cost by category, AI calls and cost per call): use it for questions about cost, spend or what is costing the most. For "most" / "largest", use economics-operating-cost@1's largestMeasuredCategory part (the largest MEASURED category, server-computed); its totalUsd is the sum of the categories, never a category.

function.name: get_metric
function.description: Read one metric's value envelope: metric (its key), value (or null), status, reason, window, freshness, basis.kind ("estimated" or "measured"), drill.page (a link to the page with that figure's records), window_phrase (the period these figures actually cover, in words you may quote), asked_period_available (present when the question names a period: false ⇒ this metric does not cover that period, so never say its figures do; when another of its windows does, asked_period_window names it), placeholder / placeholders (figures) and labelPlaceholder / labelPlaceholders (names). To state a figure, copy the placeholder string from this result verbatim ("placeholder", or the part's entry in "placeholders") — never the number itself, and never a placeholder you typed (the form is {{m:<metric>|part=<name>|window=<days>}}; copy it, don't build it). To name the metric or a category, copy its label placeholder ({{l:…}}) the same way. Link drill.page, never drill.href.

id.description: A metric id from list_metrics, e.g. "provider-outcome@1" or "economics-operating-cost@1".

window.description: Days, ONLY one of THIS metric's listed `windows` (list_metrics); a window it does not list is not read and you are told its windows. Omit for the default or a fixed window. "Today" is not a window: omit it, or use the metric's smallest listed window.

function.name: find_page
function.description: Find Platform pages you may open, by words in their label.

function.name: open_page
function.description: Get the link (a relative href) for one page id from find_page, optionally with its filters.

function.name: find_page
function.description: Find Platform pages you may open, by words in their label.

function.name: open_page
function.description: Get the link (a relative href) for one page id from find_page, optionally with its filters.

function.name: recall_memory
function.description: Read OPERATOR MEMORY: with no id, the index of remembered items injected in this turn; with an id, that one item. Each has its type, the live subject label, concern, the operator's note, a {{mem:<id>}} placeholder for when it was noted, and the live check (UNCHANGED, CHANGED, UPDATED or UNVERIFIED). It never returns a value: for current state, read the live metric or page.

function.name: propose_memory
function.description: Propose ONE item for the operator to remember (they confirm it; nothing is saved by you). subjectRef must be a metric key or page id you read in THIS turn. At most one per turn; end your answer normally — the server shows the confirm card.

note.description: A short note in your own words (no numbers, amounts, names, emails or ids, and never a sentence copied from the conversation).

function.name: list_customer_attention
function.description: Customers who need help now (Customer Success), most reasons first, ≤10. Each record: handle, ref, reason (primary), reasons (count), testAccount. Optional reason filters to one reason.

function.name: list_recently_joined
function.description: Customers who registered in the last `days` (default 14), newest first, ≤10. Each record: handle, ref, joinedAt, stage, importHealth, connections, invited.

function.name: get_customer_profile
function.description: One customer's status by handle (from a customers tool result or a [customer h_…] in the question): joinedAt, stage, presence, lastActive, connections, brokenConnections, openIncidents, aiTurns30d, lastEngagedAt, deactivated.

function.name: incident_overview
function.description: Incident counts now: brokenNow, needsVerification, bySeverity, byDomain, widespread, customerActionable, causeStatus. No records.

function.name: list_incidents
function.description: Platform Ops incidents, most urgent first, ≤10, identity-free: handle + state, severity, domain, kind, operation, times, spread, causeStatus, cause. State a cause as fact ONLY when causeStatus is CONFIRMED (and place the incident {{r:h|ref}} in that sentence); otherwise wrap it in {{inferred}}…{{/inferred}}.

function.name: investigate_incident
function.description: One incident by handle (a list result or [incident h_…]): + displayStatus, remedy, providerErrorCode, attempts, recovery, closure, last action/outcome codes.

function.name: list_incidents_cs
function.description: Customer Success view of list_incidents: + customer (user # ref). Place the customer with {{r:h|name}}.

function.name: investigate_incident_cs
function.description: Customer Success view of investigate_incident (+ customer).

function.name: onboarding_overview
function.description: Onboarding counts: new-connection imports (7 d) by status / failed reason; with Customer Success also needsHelp (per onboarding reason, link codes, funnel stages, nextSteps text). No records.

function.name: list_onboarding_attention
function.description: Customers who need onboarding help (Customer Success), ≤10: handle, ref, reason, reasonAt, registeredAt, linkErrorCode, addFailureStage, importReason, otherReasons, testAccount. Optional reason filter.

function.name: get_onboarding_timeline
function.description: One customer's onboarding by handle: registeredAt, invited, verifiedAt, firstSessionAt, stage, bank / wallet connections, imports by status, lastImportFailure, firstWealthRegenAt, firstAiTurnAt, firstBriefAt.

function.name: connection_health_overview
function.description: Connection health counts (banks + wallets): total, byHealth, retired, bySource faults by healthState + errorCode, unhealthy by institution / wallet network code. No records, no customers.

function.name: get_customer_connections
function.description: One customer's live connections by customer handle, ≤10: provider, kind, institution, network (wallet chain code), status, healthState, errorCode, needsReauth, lastSyncedAt, neverSynced, connectedAt.
